title: Retro game reconstruction discovery
summary: Review 25 game reconstruction, disassembly and port projects across Amiga, DOS, Commodore 64 and ZX Spectrum.
notes: Personally reviewed pinned primary READMEs and screened repository URLs against the current main catalogue. No independent build, execution or byte comparison. Project scope and upstream claims are bounded to the stated evidence.

sources.reason: C++/SDL2 modernization of the completed GameReverse recreation, explicitly building on that project rather than an independent original-game reconstruction.
Source-derived Gloom PC port, with original Amiga source and assets described as gameplay authority. Distinct port rather than a claim of binary-derived original source recovery.

Rebuilds several PC executables against original tools; README distinguishes reconstructed game code from generated assembly stand-ins and original library components. Exactness is an upstream claim, not independent verification.

DOS executable used as an oracle in a staged recovery port with a generated VMless frontend and an authored gameplay region. Oracle and hybrid workbench modes remain distinct from the recovered composition.
Game-specific PortForge target using the original executable as an oracle and recovering behavior against it. Current status and any native-completion claims are bounded to upstream documentation.
Historical C/ASM reconstruction of a specified PRINCE.EXE revision. Component matching is underway; whole-link closure is a separate investigation and no SDL port is claimed.
C reimplementation of the 1993 DOS game from documented original assembler, with real-hardware and trace layers and a Turbo C build workflow. Treat author equivalence claims as unverified.
C64 recovery project using c64_re with the original disk as an oracle, game-specific adapter and boot/play evidence. The README describes a bring-up stage, not a complete native port.
Reconstructs UGH.EXE using hand assembly and C with original runtime components. README reports full-file matching through historical build and pack tools; not independently reproduced.
Rust/WebAssembly reimplementation based on analysis of DOS executables and manuals, loading original game data. Upstream documents campaign and battle implementation.
Experimental portable C port based on decompilation and original game assets. Author aims for mostly faithful game logic, not byte-identical DOS reconstruction.
SkoolKit disassembly of the ZX Spectrum game; the author provides a browsable listing and an HTML build recipe.
Spectrum-native Z80 port of C64 Revs+ simulation, compared against emulated C64 execution; BBC source also informed the work. New renderer and memory layout are Spectrum-specific.
Commodore 1351 mouse patch, reverse-engineering notes and partial native C128 port of Bryan Brandenburg’s Sentinel, not Geoff Crammond’s The Sentinel.
C/SDL2 rewrite of the Aquatic Adventure pinball table using the original Amiga AQUA.BIN data; this is one table, not a complete game remake.
Browser reconstruction of Stunts with original DOS data preparation and multiple edition support. README describes reconstructed TypeScript, not running the DOS executable.
Unity remake using original game data; credits BaKGL and canassa’s reconstruction as references and Spice86 for side-by-side comparison. Separate implementation, not original-source recovery.
TypeScript/Three.js reimplementation and editor for the LBA games using imported game data. The reviewed README does not establish which original platform binaries were analysed.
Free in the Dark is a modern engine reimplementation targeting several Alone in the Dark releases. Specific source binary/platform provenance is not established from the inspected README.
Routine-by-routine Rust port of DOS ACD.EXE checked against an emulated original, with a new wgpu frontend; author fidelity claims are not independently verified.
C/SDL2 reimplementation of two DOS games from reading their original programs, with unpackers and Ghidra scripts. Upstream reports beta scope and remaining unsupported modes.
SilverMachine alpha reimplements the game from original user-supplied DOS data; upstream credits other source reconstructions as references rather than copied code.
SkoolKit disassembly and recovered Sinclair BASIC listing of the Spectrum game, which is mostly BASIC with a small machine-code stub.
SkoolKit disassembly of the ZX Spectrum game The Trap Door, with a published annotated listing.

Author describes a fully documented Spectrum Cobra reconstruction informed by Spectrum Analyser and discussions with its original programmer; the README’s completeness claim is not independently tested.
